header: Levy Brands LLC and its affiliated operating companies, including TaliWood Cabinets, LLC. Terms and Conditions of Sale.
lead: These Terms govern every sale by Levy Brands LLC and its affiliated operating companies, including TaliWood Cabinets, LLC, and are incorporated into every quotation, order acknowledgment, order confirmation, invoice and delivery. The Seller on any given sale is the entity that issues the invoice for it. See Section 1.2.
footer: Levy Brands LLC and affiliated operating companies, including TaliWood Cabinets, LLC. 10450 Greens Crossing Blvd, Houston, TX 77038. Product and quality claims: claims@levybrands.com. Billing and invoice disputes: accounting@taliwood.com.
version_rule: This page always shows the current version. The version that applies to a sale is the version in effect on the date Seller accepted the order, not the version shown here today. Each version stays available at its own permanent address and is never edited after publication.

appendices.5.9: This Section is a condition precedent only to an action by Buyer. It does not apply to, does not delay, and is not a condition precedent to any action by Seller for the price or to collect or enforce any amount owed, or to any application by Seller for a writ or other provisional remedy, and Buyer may not demand or invoke reinspection to postpone or defend against such an action.

clauses.1.1: These Terms govern every sale by Levy Brands LLC and by each of its subsidiaries and affiliated operating companies, including TaliWood Cabinets, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company with its principal place of business at 10450 Greens Crossing Blvd, Houston, TX 77038, and are incorporated into every quotation, order acknowledgment, order confirmation, invoice and delivery issued by any of them.
clauses.1.2: Who the Seller is. "Seller" means the single legal entity that issues the invoice for the sale in question. Where the invoice is issued by TaliWood Cabinets, LLC, TaliWood Cabinets, LLC is the Seller for that sale and is the only contracting party for it. Where the invoice is issued by Levy Brands LLC or by another subsidiary or affiliated operating company, that entity is the Seller for that sale and is the only contracting party for it. If a quotation or order confirmation names one entity and the invoice for the same goods names another, the entity named on the invoice is the Seller.
clauses.1.3: Brands and product lines are not the Seller. TaliWood, EZ Click, Plywood Source, Primo Ply and any other brand, product line, division, trade name or assumed name used by Seller is a name only. It is not a legal person, it is not the Seller, it does not contract, and no obligation is owed by it or to it. EZ Click is a product line of TaliWood Cabinets, LLC and is not a separate seller. Each sale is a separate contract with the one entity that issues the invoice for it. No entity is liable for the obligations of any other entity under these Terms. Buyer may not combine invoices issued by different entities for any purpose, may not apply a claim against one entity to a balance owed to another, and may not treat a course of dealing, waiver, credit or accommodation given by one entity as binding on another.
clauses.1.6: Product scope. The provisions of these Terms that refer to grading, published grade standards, origin or load-port inspection, mill grading or grading certificates, piece tallies, falldown, off-grade or mill-run goods, and further manufacturing such as cutting, ripping, sanding or laminating apply only to plywood, panel, veneer and lumber products. Cabinets and cabinet components are sold under the remaining provisions of these Terms, together with any terms and conditions of sale for cabinet products that Seller publishes, which control for those products where they differ from these Terms.
clauses.5.14: Limitations period. (a) Buyer's actions. ANY ACTION BY BUYER ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO A SALE, THE GOODS, OR THESE TERMS MUST BE COMMENCED WITHIN ONE (1) YEAR AFTER DELIVERY. The parties agree that this is a reduction of the period of limitation by the original agreement of the parties under Tex. Bus. & Com. Code 2.725(a), that one year is a reasonable period, and that it applies to every claim, cause of action, counterclaim, cross-claim, defense in the nature of a claim, and third-party claim Buyer may assert, however characterized, including breach of contract, breach of warranty, nonconformity, shortage, delay, misrepresentation, negligence, and any statutory claim. If a one-year period is unenforceable under applicable law, the period is the shortest enforceable period and in no event more than two (2) years after delivery. (b) Seller's actions are not shortened. Nothing in this Section, and nothing anywhere in these Terms, shortens the time for any action by Seller. Seller has the full period allowed by applicable law, and in no event less than four (4) years, to commence any action for the price of goods sold, or to collect or enforce any invoice, account, open or stated account, account balance, unpaid principal, finance charge, service charge, late charge, interest, returned-item fee, collection cost, court cost or attorney fee, or to enforce any credit agreement, guaranty, security agreement, security interest, letter of credit or other credit support, or to recover goods or proceeds. Every reduction of a limitations period in these Terms applies only to actions by Buyer. (c) No reciprocity. Buyer acknowledges that the reduction in (a) is part of the allocation of risk reflected in the price under Section 7.5, that it is not conditioned on any reciprocal reduction, and that it is enforceable although it applies only to Buyer. Buyer waives any argument that the period in (a) must be applied to Seller, and any argument that (b) makes (a) unenforceable. If a court holds that (a) cannot apply to Buyer unless it also applies to Seller, then (a) is void and Buyer's claims are governed by the longest period that leaves (b) intact.
clauses.5.15: Billing disputes and goods claims are separate, with separate deadlines and separate addresses. (a) Billing dispute. A dispute about the amount billed rather than the condition or conformity of the goods is a billing dispute. Billing disputes include price, price extension, unit of measure, quantity billed, freight, fuel and accessorial charges, tax, discount, rebate, program credit, credit memo, duplicate billing, misapplied payment, and application of a payment. A billing dispute is governed solely by the invoice-dispute provision of the credit agreement signed by Buyer and Seller, and notice of it must be received in writing within the period that credit agreement states, at the billing address stated in that credit agreement or, if none is stated, at accounting@taliwood.com. Where there is no signed credit agreement, notice of a billing dispute must be received in writing at that billing address within fifteen (15) days after the invoice date, after which the invoice is final and binding on Buyer. (b) Goods claim. A claim that the goods are nonconforming, short, damaged, mis-shipped, off-grade, defective, incomplete, or otherwise not what was ordered is a goods claim. A goods claim is governed solely by this Section 5, must be received at the claims address in 5.2, and must meet the periods in 5.3 and 5.4 and the conditions in 5.7 and 5.8. An invoice-dispute period in a credit agreement does not create, extend, restart, replace or toll any period in this Section 5, and does not create any right to withhold payment. (c) Each notice goes to its own address. A writing delivered to the billing address does not start or toll any period under this Section 5, and a writing delivered to the claims address does not start or toll any invoice-dispute period under a credit agreement. A single writing may raise both a billing dispute and a goods claim only if it separately states the amount disputed as a billing matter and separately identifies the pieces claimed as a goods matter with the information required by 5.2, and is received at both addresses within the shorter of the two applicable periods. (d) The two periods do not interpret each other. The periods in this Section 5 and any invoice-dispute period in a credit agreement are independent, are measured from different events, and each is enforceable on its own terms. Buyer may not argue that the difference between them makes either one ambiguous, inapplicable, extended or unenforceable. Where the same facts could be presented as either, the shorter period controls and the requirements of 5.2, 5.7 and 5.8 apply. (e) Payment is still due. Neither a billing dispute nor a goods claim entitles Buyer to withhold, offset, deduct or delay payment. Section 10.3 applies to both.
clauses.10.1: Payment terms. Payment is due net 30 days from the invoice date, unless different payment terms are stated in a credit agreement signed by Buyer and by an officer of Seller, in which case that credit agreement controls. Payment is measured from the invoice date. It is not measured from the date of shipment, delivery, receipt, inspection, installation, completion of a job, or the date Buyer is paid by its own customer or by any builder, contractor or other person.
clauses.10.2: A document does not change the signed terms. Payment terms, due dates, discount terms or late-charge terms printed or displayed on an invoice, statement, packing list, order confirmation, quotation, portal screen, emailed summary, or any other document generated by Seller or by Buyer do not add to, vary, extend or waive the payment terms in a signed credit agreement or in Section 10.1. Where such a document shows terms more favorable to Buyer than the signed terms, it is an error, it does not extend the due date, it does not waive any late charge, and Buyer may not rely on it. Only a writing signed by an officer of Seller changes payment terms. No salesperson, sales representative, agent, customer-service employee or credit employee may change them. Where there is no signed credit agreement, Section 10.1 applies unless Seller has agreed in writing to prepayment, cash in advance, letter of credit or other terms for that order. Past-due balances accrue service charges at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum lawful rate, or at the rate stated in a signed credit agreement if that agreement states a different rate.
clauses.12.4: Sections 1.2, 1.3, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10.3 and 12 survive delivery, acceptance, payment and any termination or cancellation. Section 5.14(b) survives without limitation.
clauses.13.1: Versioning. Each version of these Terms carries a version number and an effective date, and is published at its own permanent address. Seller does not edit a published version. A change is made by publishing a new version with a new number and a new effective date.
clauses.13.2: Which version applies. The version that governs a sale is the version in effect on the date Seller accepted the order for that sale. A later version does not apply to an order Seller accepted before that version's effective date, and does not change any claim period, deadline, remedy or limitation that had already begun to run.
clauses.13.3: Availability. Seller keeps every prior version available at its permanent address and will provide a copy of any version on written request.

Product scope clarified for plywood, panel, veneer and lumber products and for cabinets and cabinet components (1.6). Version 1.0, effective August 25, 2026, levybrands.com/terms/v1-0.
